settings.title: The largest hands-on learning campus in the world.

settings.description_text: Run real experiments yourself. Feel the "Aha!" you want for your students before they do.
27 years. 40 million children reached. 300,000 teachers trained. Built to nurture curiosity, creativity and confidence — the world's largest hands-on learning campus.
Founders, principals and academic heads only. The group is kept intentionally small, so the three days lead to genuine outcomes and lasting connections.

settings.title: Every child is naturally curious. Education should build on that.

settings.editor:
That belief started Agastya in 1999, when Ramji Raghavan brought together a group of scientists, educators and entrepreneurs around a single idea: children learn through hands-on exploration, and rote memorisation quietly takes that away from them.

Today we're one of India's leading education non-profits, and what we call the world's largest creativity laboratory - reaching over 40 million children and 300,000+ teachers across 24 states, through mobile science labs, innovation hubs, campus creativity labs, science centres and digital learning platforms.

THE PROVOCATION
See what AI is already doing inside classrooms — then map, honestly, what it takes from your school in five years, and the short list it never will.

THE IMMERSION
You become the student. Labs, experiments, your own hands. Then build an experiential lesson your teachers can run next week.

THE COMMITMENT

Full session-by-session agenda drops soon. Registered leaders see it first.

settings.title: The children speak first. You listen.

settings.editor: A circle of Agastya's Young Instructor Leaders sits at the centre of the room and talks about how they actually learn, what school gets wrong, and what they want from the adults deciding their future.
The principals sit outside the circle. No questions. No corrections. For thirty minutes, you only listen.

settings.title: We're curating a global faculty with distinguished work in AI and education.
Over three days, you'll learn from the voices redefining what school is for.
From the labs building the tools your school is now weighing up — and the researchers studying what they do to learning.
A world-renowned voice on how children learn
Whose work has reshaped classrooms across the globe — and answers this room's question better than almost anyone.
School leaders who've already rebuilt around curiosity — and have the results to prove it works.

Dean of Parents, Alpha School

Heather leads the family side of Alpha School, the AI-powered, student-led school in the US where children finish core academics in just two hours a day, and score in the nation's top percentiles. It's one of the most talked-about experiments in world education. Across 25 years she's been a teacher, a founding principal, and a superintendent leading 13 campuses — and once lifted results 40% in a single year on a high-poverty campus. At the Conclave, she unveils what an AI-powered school looks like

Professor, School of Data Science & AI, IIT Madras

An expert in data science, AI and systems control, Prof. Tangirala teaches at IIT Madras and IIT Tirupati, where he serves as Dean of Competency Development and Outreach. He is Chief Coordinator of SWAYAM PRABHA, the Ministry of Education's large-scale digital learning initiative, and Editor-in-Chief at the Institution of Engineers (India), with 100+ published papers and national recognition for teaching and research. At the Conclave, he brings the researcher's clarity to what AI can and can't do for how children learn.

Co-Founder, The Accelerated School

Sandeep Srivastava is Co-Founder of The Accelerated School, an author, and AI-age education thinker. He advocates human-centred, accelerated K-12 learning through deep reading, mathematics, academic mastery, and self-learning resources. Having home-educated his daughter, he developed nearly 100 self-learning books and 5,000+ mathematical concepts. His vision combines AI-ready education, independent learning, innovative governance, and dignified living through accessible, personalised education.His work aims to redefine schooling by combining AI-enabled education, foundational knowledge, and accessible learning resources.

President, Catalign Innovation Consulting

Vinay teaches innovation and design thinking at IIM Bangalore and IIT Bombay, and is the co-author of 8 Steps to Innovation: Going from Jugaad to Excellence (HarperCollins). For nearly two decades, he has helped organisations and leaders build a genuine culture of innovation through 100+ hands-on workshops on design thinking and creative problem-solving. His work focuses on the human skills that matter most as AI reshapes the classroom.

Vikram Sarabhai Distinguished Professor, ISRO Former Chairman

Dr. Alur Seelin Kiran Kumar is a distinguished Indian space scientist with over four decades of experience at ISRO. He served as Chairman of ISRO, the Space Commission and Secretary, Department of Space from 2015 to 2018. He previously served as Director of the Space Applications Centre (SAC), Ahmedabad, and made significant contributions to the development of Chandrayaan-1 and the Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan).  A recipient of the Padma Shri in 2014, he is a Fellow of the Indian National Academy of Engineering.

Senior Staff Research Engineer, Deepmind Google

Dr Ajit Narayanan is a Senior Staff Research Engineer at Google DeepMind, Bangalore, where he leads some initiatives on AI and the future of education. Prior to his role at Google DeepMind, Ajit was a technical lead in Google Accessibility, focusing on making Google products work better for people with disabilities like dyslexia and autism. His work at Avaz led to several awards, including the National Award for Empowerment of People with Disabilities from the President of India, being named the Innovator of the Year by MIT TR35, and being invited to give a TED talk.

Executive Vice-Chairman, Agastya International Foundation

A chemical engineer from IIT Madras with an MBA from IIM Ahmedabad, Thiagarajan spent over three decades leading companies across engineering, IT and infrastructure — as President, MD and CEO — before bringing that operating discipline to Agastya. For 16 years he has run the foundation's operations and scale, growing it into one of India's largest education movements. He has taught and spoken at the IITs, IIMs, ISB, and Kellogg, and serves on CII's national committees.

Professor, Dean (R&D) & Head – Department of Data Science & Artificial Intelligence (IIIT-Bangalore)

Prof. Dinesh Babu Jayagopi is a Professor at IIIT Bangalore, where he serves as Dean of Research & Development and Head of the Department of Data Science & Artificial Intelligence (DSAI).  He holds a Ph.D. from École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), Switzerland, and has received several prestigious recognitions, including the National Teachers Award from the President of India in 2023, the Outstanding Paper Award at ICMI 2012 and the Idiap Best PhD Student Research Award.

Founder, Agastya International Foundation

In 1998 he left a banking career across Citibank in India, Puerto Rico and New York to start Agastya — and spent the next 27 years building it into what is now the world's largest hands-on learning campus, reaching over 40 million children and 300,000 teachers. He has served on the Government of India's Central Advisory Board of Education, and spoken at Stanford, MIT Media Lab, the Clinton Global Initiative and the Education World Forum. Under his chairmanship, Agastya won the Google Global Impact Award and was ranked among the Rockefeller Foundation's top 100 global innovators.
